blocks.content: The Constitution of India is the supreme law of India.

items: Questions frequently test emergency provisions under Articles 352, 356, and 360.
Remember the distinction between Fundamental Rights (justiciable) and DPSPs (non-justiciable).
Pay special attention to amendments added by the 42nd and 44th Constitutional Amendment Acts.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.
Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution from Articles 12 to 35.
Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are contained in Part IV from Articles 36 to 51.
